summary: The note describes how local manufacturers have been adopting automation and robotics since September 1, 2023, and argues that robots complement rather than replace workers. It covers cost barriers for SMEs, modular robotics, government incentives, workforce retraining, productivity and quality gains at Atlas Component Systems, small-batch customization, and robotics spreading into agriculture, hospitality and healthcare.
one_line: Local manufacturers are adopting robotics and automation to boost productivity, customization and competitiveness while retraining workers and extending into non-traditional sectors.
key_facts: Since September 1, 2023, the local manufacturing sector has seen a marked shift toward advanced robotics and automation solutions.

Johnathan Meyers, CEO of MeyTech Industries, says "These machines aren't replacing our workforce; they're empowering them," with employees overseeing robotic systems that handle repetitive, high-precision jobs.
Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) face the biggest initial barriers to automation, namely cost and scaling issues.
Lydia Rivers, who runs a boutique automotive parts company, started with one robotic arm and now has a cluster of robots, using modular robotics that can be easily reconfigured for different tasks.
Tax breaks and innovation grants are increasingly available to ease the financial strain on SMEs adopting automation.
Vocational training centers and community colleges offer courses in robotics maintenance, programming, and operations.
Marcus Lee, a former textile worker, retrained and moved into a role in robotic maintenance.
Atlas Component Systems reported a 30% increase in output in late 2023 after implementing smart assembly-line robots, and production errors fell by 70%.
Hanna Zimmerman, Atlas' Chief Operation Officer, says robotic systems achieve a level of precision not feasible with an entirely human workforce.
Jameson Goods, a producer of high-end sports equipment, offers custom design options with fast turnaround times, according to Rebecca Kirkland, head of product development.
Robotics are being adopted in agriculture, hospitality and healthcare, including urban farming, automated planting and harvesting, and telepresence robots assisting patient care.
Investment in digital infrastructure and smart technologies has been at an all-time high since late 2023.
Dr. Trent Kowalski, a local tech philosopher, calls the shift societal and possibly the largest transformation in production and consumption since the industrial revolution.
Elena Vargas of Vargas Textile Solutions says, "To keep pace, let alone lead, you have to think big."
